newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise, Nasdaq above 1,500 for first time.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise, Nasdaq above 1,500 for first time.

text.p: Stocks finished the week on a positive note Friday in a rally paced by solid gains in computer and high-technology issues that pushed the Nasdaq composite index above 1,500 for the first time.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 35.06 points to 7,921.82, about 40 points below Tuesday's record close of 7,962.31. For the week, the Dow gained 26.01 points.

The Nasdaq index, laden with tech stocks, jumped 11.69 to 1,502.62, its seventh consecutive record. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,720 to 1,069 on heavy volume of 499 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Wall Street was again in a bullish mood after the government reported that wholesale prices fell for an unprecedented six straight month in June. The 0.1 percent drop in producer prices followed a 0.3 percent decline in May.

The news sparked a jump in bonds, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury adding 15/32, or $4.69 on a $1,000 bond, to yield 6.53 percent, dowm from 6.56 percent Thursday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.

Analysts said several factors fuelled the rally in computer shares. One was Compaq Computer Corp.'s strong earnings report on Thursday, which investors said was a good omen for the group. Compaq jumped 3-7/8 to 124 and Dell Computer surged 9-3/8 to 138.

"People have had the jitters for second-quarter technology numbers and then Compaq comes in," said Daniel Kunstler at J.P. Morgan. "What's going on is an interpretation that what's going on with Compaq has got to be good for Dell too."

Also, as tech stocks climbed again some investors began to show signs of pulling back from blue chips, producing a choppy market that saw the Dow fail in several attempts at the 8,000-point milestone.

"We keep flirting with the 8,000 level and we keep getting shot down," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "This may mean the market will continue to face this kind of volatile consolidation just below 8,000."
But analysts said investors were still committed to pouring funds into U.S. financial assets.

"The Federal Reserve has managed to keep the economy on a slow, steady growth path with little or no inflation," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates. "Where else would you go but into dollar-denominated assets if you were a portfolio manager with excess liquidity?"
Earnings news dominated the action among individual issues. Crown Cork & Seal Co. slid 6-7/16 to 49-15/16 after the company's second-quarter results fell short of estimates.

MCI Communications Corp. tumbled 7-3/8 to 35 after warning its earnings for this and next year would likely fall short of Wall Street estimates. The company blamed delays in gaining access to U.S. local phone service markets.

The announcement also cast doubt on whether MCI's planned acquisition by British Telecommunications would occur on the terms originally set for the deal. American Depositary Shares in British Telecom fell 5-1/4 to 76-5/16.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.90 points to 916.68. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.77 to 635.47.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.85 to 478.12. The average share was up 17 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,682.697, up 40.419 or 0.47 percent.
